findings: P1 authority/identity-binding: terminal_statuses_if_approved matches bundles with unanchored b.endswith(rb); a path whose tail string-matches another node's results_bundle (e.g. 'myresults/047' vs 'results/047') inherits that node's terminal completion authority. Require a path boundary: b == rb or b.endswith('/' + rb).

P1 CI-gate consistency: check.yml enforces `scout.py state-verify --require-all`, but CI_PROVENANCE_CORRECTION_20260906.md in the same commit reports a reproducible stale idea_card_sha256/source_fingerprint_sha256 view in ideas 023/045/046 with those state files deliberately preserved. Either the shipped gate is red on the shipped tree or state-verify does not check the fingerprint the code documents; regenerate the state files via the sanctioned refresh (doc confirms no node status or approval changes, so approvals are preserved) or reconcile the gate.

P2 privacy surface: fetch_provenance's `git fetch --depth=1 origin <sha>` materializes the full snapshot tree of the results-branch commit (every blob, not only the bound HUMAN_APPROVED_PROBE) into the CI/local object store; prefer --filter=blob:none so only the single sha256-verified blob is fetched on demand. The contaminated-source guard also blocks only the one exact commit sha, not other snapshots embedding the same bytes — acceptable only while manifest entries stay review-gated.

P2 doc/code divergence: derive_status accepts registry-declared terminal_statuses as terminal evidence without the A3 approval-binding gate (the gate exists only in terminal_statuses_if_approved), so an unapproved registry edit can steer a node into the terminal branch of derive_status/state_summary; mitigated by pin attestation and bundle validation but contradicts the module header's authority statement.

P3 robustness: derive_status raises unhandled exceptions instead of reporting findings on wrong-shaped inputs — summary.json parsing to a JSON list hits AttributeError on summary.get, and an artifact dependency resolving to a directory makes artifact_issues' read_bytes raise IsADirectoryError.

P3 test portability: test_exact_missing_object_retrieved_without_branch_history fetches a non-advertised sha from a file:// remote, relying on protocol v2's unrestricted wants; it fails if protocol.version is forced below 2 — set uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant=true on the fixture source repo to pin the behavior.

Sound (no change requested): GIT_OBJECT_UNAVAILABLE vs GIT_PATH_UNAVAILABLE split fails closed without disproving approvals; exact-SHA depth-1 retrieval with byte verification, closed manifest schema, and locked marker path; no ref/HEAD mutation (test-asserted); __SUPERSEDED__ ratification rows confer nothing silently while forged current-bytes rows fail loudly; publication audit remains read-only with the delta files correctly allowlisted.
